A 2x2 grid sheet: four separate square panels separated by thick plain gutters of the same flat background color. Each panel holds one head-and-shoulders portrait, the character centered and facing slightly toward the viewer, the whole head visible with a clear margin around it.
Panel order: top-left Guan Yu (deep red face, long flowing black beard down to the chest, green headscarf and green robe, calm half-closed eyes); top-right Zhang Fei (dark ruddy face, wild spiky black beard like tiger whiskers, huge round glaring eyes, mouth wide open shouting); bottom-left Cao Cao (pale white face, thin pointed mustache and goatee, narrow scheming eyes, black official hat, faint smirk); bottom-right Lu Bu (fierce warrior, tall headdress with two very long pheasant tail feathers curving back, red lacquered armor).
Tone: B-movie comedy. Expressions are pushed to theatrical exaggeration, but proportions stay adult and realistic-ish: not chibi, not cute, not mascot-like.
Rendering: a Ming-dynasty hand-printed woodblock novel illustration (xiuxiang portrait plate). Carved black outlines of uneven width with small nicks and breaks; flat color areas in a limited palette of vermilion, indigo, ochre, muted jade green and off-black, printed slightly misregistered so color spills past the lines in places; visible paper fiber texture; shading only with a few carved hatching lines. Background: flat warm off-white paper.
Avoid: glossy digital painting, airbrushed smooth skin, rim lighting, glowing edges, bokeh, lens blur, god rays, sparkles, perfect symmetry, 3D render look, plastic sheen, gradient backgrounds, intricate filigree, fantasy game splash art look. No text, no letters, no seals, no signatures, no frames.
